sentence: at a six hour day, a year already holds about fourteen hundred and sixty days

sentence: At forty-five degrees north you move at seventy percent of the equator's speed and the push outward is only half as strong.
claim: At 45° north your speed is 71% of the equator's and the outward push on you is 50%.
note: DERIVATION: arithmetic only; not read from any page. OPEN until a person re-does the sum.
derivation: cos 45 = 0.71 for the speed; the outward push on the vertical scales as cos^2 = 0.50.

note: DERIVATION: arithmetic only; not read from any page. OPEN until a person re-does the sum.

sentence: The oceans: the water wants to be higher at the equator than at the poles; it drains toward an equatorial belt
claim: The faster Earth spins, the higher the sea wants to stand at the equator compared with the poles: 33 km higher at a 12 h day, and far more as the day gets shorter.
note: DERIVATION: arithmetic only; not read from any page. OPEN until a person re-does the sum.
derivation: Extra rise (compared with today) of the sea's equipotential at the equator relative to the pole = (w^2 - w0^2) R^2 / (2 g0): 33 km at a 12 h day, 165 km at 6 h, 692 km at 3 h; far more than the mean ocean depth (c18), so the water drains toward the equator. First-order only: it ignores the self-gravity of the water and the slow response of the ground; the direction is the claim, not the numbers.
